description.narrative: Bidraget tar upp strukturella utmaningar på arbetsmarknaden i Bosnien och Hercegovina som oproportionerligt påverkar arbetsresultaten för kvinnor, ungdomar och utsatta individer. Åtgärden arbetar med att förbättra utformningen, genomförandet och genomförandet av aktiva arbetsmarknadspolitiker med tonvikt på inriktning och antagande/diversifiering av portföljerna, vilket möjliggör utformning och genomförande av program för långtidsarbetslösa och svåranställda kategorier i samarbete med relevanta intressenter .

The contribution addresses structural labor market challenges in Bosnia and Herzegovina that disproportionally affect labor outcomes of women, youth and vulnerable individuals. The action works on improving the design, implementation and performance of active labor market policies with emphasis on targeting and adoption/diversification of the portfolios, enabling the design and implementation of programs for long-term unemployed and hard to employ categories in cooperation with relevant stakeholders.

During the reporting period 01 February 2023 to 31 January 2024, the project measured a series of expected results in line with the proposed work plan. Team consisting of 9 professionals were selected and appointed with respective responsibilities to ensure smooth implementation of the project. The first four (4) months of the project were designated for the inception phase during which the project team carried out an in-depth analysis to review original description of action and introduce changes where necessary. On the basis of the analysis small changes were introduced mainly pertaining to scheduling of planned trainings of public employment services (PES) staff and respective ministry staff to ensure that it is matched with the activities relevant for that training. In addition during the inception phase, the project established a project steering board consisting of representatives of national stakeholders and donors (EU and Sweden) aimed at having a platform to share information, receive formal approval for relevant documents and actions etc. The Rule of Procedure for the work of Project Steering Board (PSB) are developed and adopted. During the reporting period PSB had three meetings that all had required quorum.
Further, part of the team that is responsible for communication and visibility, developed a communication strategy, developed a brand identify of the project and implemented a number of public campaigns mainly focused on disseminating information on grant scheme developed and launched during the reporting period.
Sticking to grant scheme the project team on the basis of detailed analysis of PES policies and registries and in cooperation with national stakeholders and donors developed an innovative grant scheme targeting vulnerable categories. More specifically the grant scheme is based on the public call allowing a flexible approach for civil society organization, local communities in cooperation with PES(s) to develop employment opportunities for respective/individual categories (youth, women in rural areas, Roma, persons with disabilities and so-called long term-unemployed persons). In the reporting period the project invested sizable efforts to conduct info sessions across the country in order to facilitate application process by those who are interested to provide required services. Following the intense work on the development of public calls, grant scheme, information sharing and capacity building, the calls were published and applications received. The evaluation of received applications is scheduled for late April.
Also in terms of expected results, the project carried out number of trainings as per the intended work plan, developed guidelines and manuals to support the work of PES(s) in terms of activation labour measures, profiling and development of programmes both on the demand and supply side of the labour market.
As a remainder the original Description of Action was developed by the EUD in BiH and it proposed the engagement of French Public Employment Services to provide technical assistance in relevant areas. Once Sweden expressed its interest to co-finance the project it was also proposed that Swedish Public Employment Services also be engaged given their experience and work carried out in the region. During the reporting period, the project made arrangements with both employment services (French and Swedish) to provide required technical assistance. Number of trainings were already completed and additional ones are planned during the project.
In conclusion when it comes to expected results the project are in line with what is anticipated and in some areas, primarily in terms of quantitative indicators, has surpassed expectations.
